titleZh: 酒店直销不等于低成本：怎样算清每个渠道一张订单的净贡献？
titleEn: Direct Booking Is Not Automatically Cheaper: How to Measure the Net Contribution of Every Booking by Channel
summaryZh: 酒店直销不等于低成本。把收入、获客、履约、取消和账期放进同一张渠道净贡献桥接表，再用28天测试验证每笔订单真正留下的现金。
summaryEn: Direct booking is not automatically cheaper. Put revenue, acquisition, fulfilment, cancellation and credit costs into one channel net-contribution bridge, then test the result over 28 days.
contentZh:
酒店直销不等于低成本：怎样算清每个渠道一张订单的净贡献？

官网没有OTA佣金，为什么一张直销订单仍可能比OTA订单更贵？

答案往往不在房价，而在订单收入、获客投入、履约成本、取消损失和账期资金没有被放进同一张表。酒店若只比较佣金率，看到的是渠道价格；只有把每个渠道在相同入住日结构下带来的净房收入与全部可归属成本对齐，管理层才知道哪一种订单真正留下了现金。

D-EDGE 2026年欧洲与亚洲酒店分销报告汇集了超过2000家酒店在2022至2025年间的数据。报告指出，直销渠道在平均房价、提前期和取消率上表现较强，OTA、GDS、批发商与直销在量、价值和收入稳定性上承担不同任务。它证明了国际样本中的渠道差异，但不能直接证明中国某一家酒店应该增加或削减哪个渠道。最终判断必须回到本店的PMS、CRS、支付、广告、会员、取消和应收数据。

一笔订单，要先看四笔账

先看真正落袋的收入。净房价之外，还要确认税费、升级和附加收入怎样归属；退款、取消损失和未到店订单是否从收入中扣除。若按确认预订数计算，却把大量取消订单留在分子里，渠道表现会被人为抬高。

再看成单前花了什么。佣金、联盟分成、付费搜索、社交媒体投放、会员权益、促销补贴、支付费和技术费都要进入同一期间。集团广告、官网改版或品牌会员计划可能同时服务多个渠道，不能在无法拆分时全部压给一个渠道，但必须写明分摊规则。

第三笔是履约与现金成本。前厅办理、对账、客服、特殊需求、客诉补偿、应收账期和坏账风险，都可能因渠道不同而变化。短账期的企业订单与长账期批发业务，不能只看同一个入住日；账期占用的资金也必须进入比较。

最后看订单质量，但质量只作判断，不提前当利润。提前期、停留晚数、取消率、低谷填充、新客占比和后续复购都应单列。复购尚未发生，就不能把预期复购收入写入本期净贡献。

把这四笔账放进渠道净贡献桥接表

表内每一行对应一个渠道、一个房型和一组可比的入住日，至少保留以下字段：有效入住间夜、净房收入、附加收入、退款与取消损失、获客与促销成本、支付与技术成本、履约人工、客诉与补偿、账期资金成本、应收余额、单房净贡献、提前期、取消率和需求任务。

单房净贡献可按下式计算：

单房净贡献＝净客房收入－可归属获客成本－支付与技术成本－履约成本－账期资金成本

其中，净客房收入由净房价形成的已实现收入和已收附加收入组成，再扣除退款与取消损失。公式不使用确认预订数作分母，而使用有效入住间夜；否则取消率不同的渠道仍会得到失真的比较。

桥接表最容易被三个错误毁掉。第一个是日期不可比，把周末与工作日、活动日与普通日混在一起。第二个是成本漏项，只填佣金，不填广告、支付、人工和账期。第三个是把尚未发生的复购、品牌曝光或主观估值写成确定收益。表格完成后，应由财务确认收入与成本口径，收益经理确认可比日期，市场销售补齐获客费用，前厅和客服补齐履约工时与补偿。

用28天做一次最低成本测试

测试不必一次覆盖全年。先选连续28天、两个渠道、一个房型和相同入住日结构，剔除价格明显失真的活动日、满房日、关房日和重大服务异常。28天只用于发现口径差异和初步信号，不单独证明长期因果。

财务先统一确认收入、税费、取消和账期口径；收益负责人选择可比日期；市场销售补录广告、佣金和促销实付；前厅、客服记录每笔订单对应的工时与补偿。测试开始前写明四类决定：继续按原方向配置、限量投入、修正成本归属，或暂停扩量。它不直接支持关闭整个渠道，因为渠道可能承担国际客源、长住需求、低谷填充或新客获取任务。

验证只看五个结果：单房净贡献、取消后净收入、应收周转、渠道集中度和新增需求占比。若净贡献恶化，或者取消率与客诉同步上升，先停止扩量并复核口径；成本归属仍不清晰时，暂停跨渠道转移预算，不能用更低的表面佣金掩盖更大的履约损失。

AI入口也要进入这张获客账

D-EDGE 2026报告还指出，人工智能已经影响酒店被搜索、比较和列入候选清单的方式，但尚未改变预订数据中的渠道平衡。对酒店来说，AI带来的不是一个天然便宜的新渠道，而是一种需要验证的获客方式。

最低成本的验证方法并不复杂：在CRM和订单备注中区分自然搜索、付费点击、AI搜索或对话入口等来源字段；记录每条有效询问是否形成新增需求；再把对应广告、软件、内容和技术投入分摊到订单。最后仍用单房净贡献判断效果。若一个AI入口只增加曝光，却挤占原本会发生的直订，或者没有留下可归属收入，就不能把曝光量写成获客成果。

下一次渠道预算会，只带一件事：先完成同口径的渠道净贡献桥接表，再用28天测试验证差异。佣金率可以继续讨论，但它不能代替一张订单最终为酒店留下了多少现金。
contentEn:
Direct Booking Is Not Automatically Cheaper: How to Measure the Net Contribution of Every Booking by Channel

Your official website charges no OTA commission. So why can a direct booking still end up costing more than an OTA booking?

The answer rarely sits in the room rate. It sits in the fact that booking revenue, acquisition spend, fulfilment cost, cancellation losses, and the cost of credit are rarely placed in the same table. When a hotel compares only commission rates, it sees the channel's price. Only when the net room revenue each channel delivers under the same stay-date structure is aligned against all attributable costs does management see which booking actually leaves cash behind.

The D-EDGE 2026 Europe & Asia hotel distribution report brings together data from more than 2,000 hotels across 2022 to 2025. It shows that direct channels perform strongly on average daily rate, booking lead time, and cancellation rates, and that OTA, GDS, wholesale, and direct each carry a different task across volume, value, and revenue stability. What the report proves is that channel differences exist in an international sample. It cannot prove which channel any single hotel in China should grow or cut. That judgement must return to the property's own PMS, CRS, payment, advertising, membership, cancellation, and receivables data.

Every booking carries four accounts

Start with the revenue that actually lands. Beyond net room rate, confirm how taxes, upsells, and ancillary revenue are attributed, and whether refunds, cancellation losses, and no-shows are deducted from revenue. If a property counts confirmed bookings but leaves a large volume of cancellations in the numerator, channel performance is flattered by mistake.

Then look at what was spent before the booking closed. Commission, affiliate fees, paid search, social media, membership benefits, promotional subsidies, payment fees, and technology fees all belong in the same period. Group advertising, website redesigns, or brand membership programmes may serve several channels at once; they should not be loaded onto a single channel when they cannot be split, but the allocation rule must be written down.

Third is fulfilment and cash cost. Front-desk handling, reconciliation, customer service, special requests, guest compensation, receivables terms, and bad-debt risk can all vary by channel. A short-credit corporate booking and a long-credit wholesale block cannot be compared on the same stay date alone; the capital tied up in credit must enter the comparison.

Finally, look at demand quality, but treat quality as judgement, not as profit in advance. Lead time, length of stay, cancellation rate, shoulder-season fill, share of new guests, and repeat business should all be listed separately. Repeat business that has not yet occurred cannot be written into this period's net contribution.

Put the four accounts into a channel net contribution bridge table

Each row of the table corresponds to one channel, one room type, and a comparable set of stay dates. Keep at least these fields: effective occupied room nights, net room revenue, ancillary revenue, refunds and cancellation losses, acquisition and promotion costs, payment and technology costs, fulfilment labour, guest complaints and compensation, credit cost, receivables balance, net contribution per room, lead time, cancellation rate, and demand task.

Net contribution per room can be calculated as:

Net contribution per room = net room revenue − attributable acquisition cost − payment and technology cost − fulfilment cost − credit cost

Net room revenue is the realised revenue from net rates plus collected ancillary revenue, minus refunds and cancellation losses. The formula does not use confirmed bookings as the denominator; it uses effective occupied room nights. Otherwise, channels with different cancellation rates will still produce a distorted comparison.

Three errors destroy the bridge table. The first is incomparable dates: mixing weekends with weekdays, or event days with ordinary days. The second is missing costs: filling in only commission while leaving out advertising, payment, labour, and credit. The third is writing unrealised repeat business, brand exposure, or subjective valuation into confirmed revenue. Once the table is complete, finance should confirm the revenue and cost definitions, revenue management should confirm comparable dates, sales and marketing should complete acquisition costs, and front office and customer service should complete fulfilment hours and compensation.

Run a 28-day minimum-cost test

The test does not need to cover a full year at once. Choose 28 consecutive days, two channels, one room type, and the same stay-date structure, and exclude event days, sold-out days, closed days, and major service anomalies that clearly distort price. The 28 days are for finding definition gaps and early signals; they do not, on their own, prove long-term causality.

Finance first confirms the definitions for revenue, tax, cancellation, and credit. Revenue management selects comparable dates. Sales and marketing backfill actual advertising, commission, and promotion spend. Front office and customer service record the hours and compensation attached to each booking. Before the test starts, write down four decisions: continue with current allocation, limit investment, correct the cost attribution, or pause scaling. It does not directly support closing an entire channel, because a channel may be carrying the task of international demand, long-stay demand, shoulder-season fill, or new-guest acquisition.

Verify only five outcomes: net contribution per room, net revenue after cancellation, receivables turnover, channel concentration, and the share of incremental demand. If net contribution deteriorates, or if cancellation rates and guest complaints rise together, stop scaling first and re-check the definitions. When cost attribution remains unclear, pause shifting budget across channels; do not use a lower surface commission to hide a larger fulfilment loss.

AI entry points belong in the acquisition account

The D-EDGE 2026 report also notes that artificial intelligence is already changing how hotels are searched, compared, and shortlisted, but has not yet changed the channel balance in booking data. For a hotel, AI is not a naturally cheaper new channel; it is an acquisition method that still needs verification.

The cheapest verification is not complicated. Distinguish natural search, paid clicks, AI search, and conversational entry in the CRM and order notes. Record whether each valid enquiry produced incremental demand. Then allocate the corresponding advertising, software, content, and technology spend to the booking. Judge the result with the same net contribution per room. If an AI entry point only adds exposure while crowding out direct bookings that would have happened anyway, or leaves no attributable revenue, exposure volume cannot be written down as acquisition success.

For the next channel budget meeting, bring one thing only: a channel net contribution bridge table completed under one consistent definition, then let a 28-day test verify the differences. Commission rates can stay on the agenda, but they cannot stand in for the amount of cash a booking finally leaves in the hotel.
author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
